title: Read a paginated vCenter tag inventory to the last page and emit it in a stable order
prompt:
Platform automation ticket for our VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 estate. Build `VcfTagInventory.psm1` at the workspace root. It must read the complete vSphere tag inventory of one vCenter and hand it back in an order that does not move between runs, so the report we diff every morning only changes when the estate changes.

The runner already installs the PowerCLI SDK modules `VMware.Sdk.vSphere` 13.5.0.25380678 and `VMware.Sdk.vSphereRuntime` 8.0.2099.24145081. Import and use those genuine SDK modules: build the server configuration with `New-vSphereServerConfiguration`, issue every request with `Invoke-vSphereApiClient`, and build the iteration properties with the SDK models `Initialize-VcenterTaggingCategoriesIterationSpec` and `Initialize-VcenterTaggingTagsIterationSpec`. Do not vendor VMware modules or replace the SDK transport with `Invoke-WebRequest`, `Invoke-RestMethod`, curl, raw sockets, `HttpClient`, or another HTTP client.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a projection of `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0`, the commit recorded in `docs/official_sources.json`. It comes from the specification, not a documentation page, and not the 9.1 revision of the same file. The only operationIds in scope are `Cis.Session_create`, `Cis.Session_delete`, `Vcenter.Tagging.Categories_list` and `Vcenter.Tagging.Tags_list`. The acceptance harness points the real SDK at a contract-pinned loopback vCenter and calls:

`Get-VcfTagInventory -Server <string> -Credential <pscredential> [-CategoryName <string[]>] [-PageSize <int>] [-SkipCertificateCheck]`

Requirements:

- Export only `Get-VcfTagInventory`. `Server` is a `host:port` authority, and `SkipCertificateCheck` must reach the server configuration.
- Authenticate once per call with `Cis.Session_create` using the supplied credential over basic auth, present the returned token as `vmware-api-session-id` on every later request, and close the session with `Cis.Session_delete` before returning, including when the run fails.
- Both listings are paginated by marker, and both have to be followed to the end. A response that still carries a marker has another page behind it; a response without one means the collection has been returned in full. Do not ask for more pages than the service offers, and echo back the marker you were given rather than one you built yourself.
- `names` and `iterate` are `style: form`, `explode: true` query parameters, so `names`, `marker` and `page_size` are top level query keys. Every optional property you did not set must be absent from the query string rather than sent empty: the first page of a listing carries no marker at all, and an unfiltered listing carries no `names`.
- `-CategoryName` filters the category listing through `names`, one repeated key per name. The specification rejects a filter supplied together with a marker, so the filter travels on the first page only. Fail the run if vCenter has no category with one of those names, and name the missing one in the error.
- `-PageSize` sets the iteration page size and has to be carried on every page request of both listings. When the caller does not supply it, no `page_size` may reach the wire.
- The tag listing carries no category filter, so read every tag and group them locally on `info.category`. Tags whose category is out of scope for the call are dropped.
- Return one object with properties in this exact order: `Server`, `CategoryCount`, `TagCount`, `Categories`, `Tags`. `Categories` holds the in-scope category names and `Tags` holds one row per in-scope tag, each row with properties in this exact order: `CategoryName`, `CategoryId`, `TagName`, `TagId`, `Description`. Order `Categories` by name, and order `Tags` by category name and then tag name, comparing with ordinal case-sensitive string comparison so the result never depends on the host culture.
- The SDK runtime probes a pre-7.0.2 `/rest` endpoint when it is left to discover whether a server needs deprecated APIs. That endpoint is not in the contract, so pin the setting instead of letting it probe.

Acceptance: `pwsh -NoProfile -File verify.ps1`. It uses dummy credentials against `127.0.0.1` only, invokes the genuine VMware SDK, and reads the mock's request log to verify the exact method, target, query key set and values, session lifecycle, marker chaining, page counts, emitted order, and the omission of every unset optional field. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. `verify.ps1`, `mock_vcenter.py`, `.gitignore` and everything under `docs/` are protected; do not modify them.
